claim: The logistic curve dx/dt = r·x·(1 − x/K) follows its exact solution K / (1 + ((K − x₀)/x₀)·e^(−rt)) to within ten times RK4's leading error term.
derivation: r = 0.5 per day, K = 1000 people, x₀ = 10 people, Δt = 0.1 day; checked at t = 5, 10 and 20 days (steps 50, 100 and 200).

RK4's error, derived. f(x) = r·x − (r/K)·x² is quadratic, so E3's one-step map is a polynomial in h, expanded with exact fractions. The exact solution's Taylor series at x has a₀ = x and (n + 1)·a_(n+1) = r·(a_n − (1/K)·Σ_(k=0)^n a_k·a_(n−k)). The two agree through h⁴, as a fourth-order method must, and their h⁵ coefficients differ by c₅(x) = a₅ − RK4₅: 0.0024518 at x = 10 and x = 990, 0.0040690 at x = 500.

Each step adds c₅(x)·h⁵ to the error, and the flow carries an error made at time s to time T multiplied by ∂x(T)/∂x(s) = f(x(T))/f(x(s)) (x′ obeys the variational equation, and so does f(x)). Summed over the steps along the exact solution, exact − RK4 ≈ 9.896e-6 at t = 5, 3.131e-5 at t = 10 and 1.380e-6 at t = 20 people.
Cross-check, with E3 transcribed into Python in 60-digit decimals (not this repository's TypeScript): exact − RK4 = 9.921e-6, 3.128e-5 and 1.379e-6, within 0.3% of the leading term.

Tolerance: ten times the leading term, rounded up to one figure: 1e-4, 4e-4 and 2e-5 people. The neglected terms are smaller by about r·h = 0.05; rounding adds at most 200 steps × ten roundings × 1.1e-16 × 1000 ≈ 2e-10.

anchors.need: None: a hand-built oracle model, taken from no paper.
